A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayesian WeakS-to-Strong research. All pages, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SciQ classification and SLURP slot-filling experiments, including ensemble, auxiliary-loss, soft-label, and cDPO results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and slot-filling results, repeated-seed comparisons, model-agreement analysis, and additional ablations in Tables 1–9 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The Bayesian EDL objective, auxiliary self-training loss, word-mediated token probabilities, and weak-model-guided cDPO procedure are retained. Joint Decoding moves from Section 4.1 to the baseline description in Section 5.2. Expanded explanations and weighting ablations do not establish a change to the proposed core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use SciQ reformulated as binary answer-correctness classification and SLURP transcriptions for generative slot filling. Added weak models and ensemble configurations do not introduce new datasets, tasks, populations, or input environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds BLOOM-1B1 and TinyLlama_v1.1 as evaluated single-model and single-weak-to-strong comparators in Tables 1–4. Naive Multi-Weak and Joint Decoding remain the ensemble baselines. The separate full hard-label comparator panel in v1 Table 4 is no longer reported.

E3.justification: v2 adds five-model ensembles alongside the original three-model configuration, plus four-model controls, generation-versus-scoring controls, weighting comparisons, and beam-size experiments with M=3, 5, and 10. Appendix C changes the stated cDPO learning rate from 2×10^-7 to 5×10^-7 and beta from 10 to 2. These substantially expand the evaluation design; dataset splits and principal metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-agreement analysis (Figure 3), staged target-token versus other-token probability ablations (Table 6), weighting-strategy comparisons (Table 7), and Joint Decoding teacher-quality and beam-size analyses (Tables 8–9). The original auxiliary-loss comparisons persist, but v1's complete hard-versus-soft-label comparison is replaced by a narrower component ablation.

E5.justification: v1 mainly reports point estimates and two classification p-value comparisons, without explicit repeated-run counts. v2 states three random seeds and reports means and standard deviations across the principal comparisons and ablations; the earlier p-value comparisons disappear. This is a substantial reporting change, but does not establish how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: Numerous retained results change: three-model Bayesian classification accuracy with auxiliary loss changes from 0.855 to 0.850±0.006, and the slot-filling ceiling changes from 0.781 to 0.748. v2 adds five-model results, including 0.866±0.006 classification accuracy and 0.724±0.015 SLU-F1 after cDPO, plus new ablation and agreement findings. Changed aggregation, ceilings, configurations, and cDPO settings preclude interpreting higher cross-version PGR values as comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: The EDL likelihood and regularizer, word-probability decomposition, cDPO objective, and PGR definition remain mathematically unchanged. The regularizer moves from Appendix B to G. v2's tokenwise teacher-forcing formula makes the existing naive generation baseline explicit; no substantive theoretical result, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Bayesian aggregation of multiple weak supervisors, extension from classification to generation, token-level soft supervision, and further improvement through cDPO. Expanded experimental support and revised terminology do not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanations of ensemble behavior: Bayesian priors provide fault tolerance, weak-model disagreement supports complementarity, TinyLlama's scoring can undermine Joint Decoding, and larger candidate pools exacerbate that failure. Appendix E additionally interprets dynamic weighting as redundant with token-level reliability information. The two-task applicability limitation remains, with the model-count limitation updated to three and five teachers.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the default beam size M=5, validation-based tuning of ceiling models and reuse of those settings, and checkpoint/license information for the added models. Appendix C updates cDPO hyperparameters while retaining most training and hardware details. Conversely, v1's explicit description of the DPO reference model and its SFT initialization is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds boosting and bagging references to the ensemble discussion, along with citations for BLOOM and TinyLlama. The existing positioning around alignment, human-opinion variability, and weak-to-strong generalization remains substantially intact. The switch to author-year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The generation and experimental sections undergo substantial reorganization: Joint Decoding moves into the baseline section, dataset and model descriptions are separated, and results are rewritten around three-versus-five-model comparisons. Probability-estimation explanations are expanded, terminology is revised, and the existing appendices are reordered around the new analyses.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive revised labels, captions, and diagram presentation, while Figure 3 adds agreement heatmaps. Main comparison tables are restructured around ensemble size and uncertainty reporting, cDPO receives a separate table, and four appendix analysis tables are added. Title styling, headings, and page headers also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis of the ensemble approach through three-seed uncertainty reporting and targeted tests of component contributions, weighting, and teacher-scoring failures. These address important gaps beyond v1's point estimates and broad hard-versus-soft comparison. The lost full hard-label panel and an inconsistent TinyLlama PGR entry in Table 4 weaken parts of the reporting, but the expanded diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement. Higher PGR under changed ceilings and settings is not itself evidence of improvement.
